requirements.statement: A notification journey's 'Add a new address' hands over to the INS address book add through today's handshake (journey-type, notification-id, fulfilment-id and handshake-token; only a registered journey type, today gbn-ag and gbn-ag-germinal-products; the return URL built on the server; the new address id handed back; cancel returns without one; no address book banner), and an unregistered journey type is refused with the INS 'Page not found'. It returns through the journey's own /address-return on the animals frontend, carrying the fulfilment id, the token, the new address id and a landing, to the page each button names: 'Save and select' commits the copy and lands on the Consignment addresses page, 'Save and return to address page' lands on the picker unselected, and 'Cancel and return to hub' is a link that saves nothing. Sam's ruling of 4 November has every link between services work from each service's own configuration, and his ruling of 27 November keeps the default that the hand-over is proved in the local and CI Docker stacks with no new CDP check.

conflicts.default: Every address needs a postcode or Zip code, whatever country is chosen, free text of at most 12 characters: 'Origin or Consignor' addresses in any MDM country and the United Kingdom-only 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' addresses are treated alike, as the germinal data fields mark the field and as the add form, the edit form and the address book API already enforce. conflicts.about: Which evidence says what the address book's add and edit do today: the INS front door and end-to-end suite extracts, or the traces taken from an earlier build.

positions.says: 'The list endpoint takes no role' described an earlier address book, not the one on main.

The add address page's heading is 'Add address details'.
Leaving the name empty shows 'Enter a name'.
The edit page is headed 'Edit address details'.
The add page is headed Add address details and has no back link.

The INS front door extract (repo:insfrontend part 5) and the end-to-end suite (repo:tests part 13), which rank above both traces, agree on today's add: the three-step add, the roles question, County on the add form, the GOV.UK validation messages, the cancel link and the edit page's wording, so the deltas in this area are measured against them. The INS fit traces (taken at INS frontend 406e300) and the end-to-end traces describe the build before the address-book theme: its 'Add address details' heading, 'Enter address details' sections, 'Enter a name' messages and phone-first edit form. They are kept as the record of that build, and the deltas name them so a reviewer can see what moved; nothing is overruled, because a stale description of a page is not something to build.

conflicts.about: Whether the add-details step holds its roles error back until the address and contact fields are valid, or shows it with them.

The service already behaves this way (repo-insfrontend-p5-079, repo-tests-p13-033), and the edit page's roles error follows the same rule (req-address-book-add-and-edit-009). prototype-dr2-1-source-p16-076 is not overruled, because its message and its link target are what req-1255 builds; only the order it checks in is set aside, and trace-prototype-dr2-1-p18-079 shows that order rather than anything else to build.

Saving the edit page without choosing a country is refused with 'Select a country' and the stored code is left as it was.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book's add-details step asks for a county.

Design Release 2.1 leaving the field out is therefore a prototype mistake, and prototype-dr2-1-source-p16-045 is set aside; req-1225, which asked for the field to go, is out of scope and keeps the claim as the record of what was set aside. trace-prototype-dr2-1-p18-116 is not overruled: it also shows the edit page's County field, which req-1226 keeps. conflicts.about: Which environments' saved addresses are deleted when the address book starts storing roles, beyond dev, test and a local stack.

conflicts.question: Besides dev, test and a local stack, which environments have their addresses collection dropped when the address book starts storing roles, and what happens to an address already saved there?
conflicts.default: After the change is released, dev and test have the whole addresses collection dropped with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and a local stack is restarted. perf-test and ext-test are dropped the same way when the change reaches them, because their addresses are test data too. Pre-production and production are not touched and no address is deleted there, the service not being live for traders yet; if an address without a role is ever found in either, it is left in place and no picker offers it, rather than being deleted or given a role.

Save and select on a hand-off gives the address the party's role without the user ticking any role, so a journey-reached add form does not ask the roles question the address-book-reached one does.
A journey section starting an address book add records where to return and suggests that section's address type.

The suite's reading that the journey form asks no roles question is set aside as a reading of the code; its proof that the party's role is saved without a tick stands, so the claim is not overruled. The prototype's journeys add addresses on their own pages and say nothing of this page, so they do not rank against it.

conflicts.about: Whether the address book has a Branch address type and a branch address role, which Design Release 2.1 and Paul's ruling have and today's services do not.

The Branch type, its role checkbox, its legend, its UK-only country and its group are built (req-1199, req-1249, req-1253, req-1220, req-1256, req-2356). The suite's claims that Branch is not offered and that five roles exist are set aside; repo-insfrontend-p5-008, repo-addressbook-p1-044 and p1-046 are not overruled, because they still correctly describe the other options, roles and groups that requirements cite.

conflicts.question: Does the edit success banner show the address's name in sentence case, as the prototype's edit banner does, or as the trader saved it, as the add banner does?
